page.layout: One page of running text, one column, with marginal notes in the left and right margins. Marginal notes stand beside lines 1, 3, 9, 10, 13 and 15. Running head at top centre. Printed page number "13" at top right. Signature "B 3" and catchword "altitudinem" at the foot. Printed number "73" at the bottom right, outside the text block.

main_text.p: oculorum, & superbia vitæ.1.Ioh.2.16. Diaboli de- [?]ludunt tris ignitura [illegible, ~12 letters] luxuriæ [illegible, ~6 letters] avaritiæ turpis lucri, & [illegible, ~8 letters] inani- gloria, Math.4.

Iam vt tròùm bastes isti perpetuò nobis insidientur, vt in æternum abripiamur exitium: nunquid nostrum est tergiversari aut segnescere, &c (vt Bæs ad lahienam saginatas aut piscicules in nassam scientes, & pendentes irruant. Sampson Philistæi sunt in insidijs, vt oculos tuos effodiant, & te captivum ducant. Et ruinpterea in meretricis alicujus Delilæ lectis aut torpescis gremio? Refert Neubrigensis deRerum Angl. quodam Ketrello nostrate Eboracensi, qui tali pollebat dono, vt diabolos quoscunque, & umbras, ac si fuissent corporea, potuerit oculis videre. O si consimili modo in conspectum prodirent nostrum, obsidentium, tentantium & oppugnantium tartarie cohortes & præsentiæ, perterriti profecto exclamaremus, cum Elisæi ministro, ad Syrorum inexpectatos Phalanges,2. Reg.6. Ps.68. Ehen Domine mi, quid faciemus? vel potius cum Davide: Salvum me fac Deus, quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam, Infixus sum in luto profundo, & non est substantia, veni in altitudinem.

page.notes: Several words in the blurred centre and left of the page are illegible and are marked. Greek and Hebrew fragments in lines 3, 4 and 5 are too faint to read and are marked as illegible. The marginal note "cap. 2." beside the Neubrigensis reference and "1.Ioh.2.16." are read from faint impressions. The left-hand note in line 5 is not read with confidence. Show-through from the reverse side affects much of the text. The printed "13" and "73" are both read as printed numbers.
